name: Topiary Engine

detectability.signature: Positron streams lacing between struts in deliberate patterns, humming on every band

proximity: Unshielded electronics stutter under its pruning-arc discharge wash
The ring visibly shears and regrows sections of its own lattice
contact: Debris entering the ring is incorporated, reshaped, and hung like espaliered wood
Discharges cripple unshielded power systems outright
prolonged_exposure: Vessels loitering too long find hull components quietly rearranged into lattice stock
Complete loss of propulsion to pruning arcs is well documented

phenomena: Exotic particles detectable on sensors venting in luminous puffs
Crystalline growth on exposed surfaces of incorporated debris
Matter spontaneously changing state within the lattice struts
hazards: Power system overload from pruning discharges
Radiation exposure exceeding safe limits near active vents
opportunities: Exotic matter collection from its forty-hour vents
Archaeological significance of an unclaimed builder culture
known_incidents: The first survey lost two drones to its pruning arcs within minutes
Three salvage syndicates have gone bankrupt attempting to harvest more than it sheds
description: A ring of sculpted exotic-matter lattice spins in the dark, its struts shaped like clipped hedges and pleached alleys, unmistakably designed. Positron streams lace between the struts in deliberate patterns, pruning and re-growing sections of itself. The whole construct fits inside a sphere of 140 kilometers, humming on every sensor band.

The Engine cycles every forty hours, venting exotic byproduct in luminous puffs and shearing off overgrown lattice with discharges that can cripple unshielded electronics. Debris that drifts into the ring is incorporated, reshaped, and hung like espaliered wood. It does not respond to hails.

Dating of its structural isotopes puts construction at roughly two centuries ago, yet no culture claims the work. The first expedition lost two drones to its pruning arcs before retreating. Fragmentary inscriptions along one strut use a script resembling Old Terran horticultural notation.

Salvage syndicates circle the Engine constantly, drawn by the exotic matter it sheds, and three have gone bankrupt trying to take more than it offers. Whether it is tending something, guarding something, or simply gardening remains unresolved. The safest view is from three million kilometers, which is exactly where most observers stay.
